rv.q: Terry Johnson's revival has energy and charm, with Tim Shortall's design evoking the period's extravagant fashions.
The Libertine is an enjoyable, but rather unfulfilling play.
Not a full-on flop all told but be warned, if you go seeking after the elixir of lusty excitement you may end up feeling you've but quaffed a cup of Earl Grey.
It is intermittently entertaining but the play never dips very deep beneath the surface.
The story of his life is shapeless and as a dramatic experience it ultimately feels a mite unsatisfying.

cn.t: Cooper brings charisma to the Earl of Rochester, but critics find this Restoration rake's story doesn't fully ignite on stage, lacking the sexiness and dramatic spark the material demands.
